interactions.title: Entrusting the Tollen business to Adam Gower
lines: DM: You're leaving 22,000 gold lighter than you entered, and without the Flaming Tempest, the various trade goods you've recovered, or any of the Skaer Steel. Some of this coin and material went to the purchase of a number of spell components for Heroes’ Feast, Greater Restoration, Raise Dead should it be necessary, and more ruby dust to restock for more Forbiddance castings, and a darkvision tattoo for Wellby, but most was left behind with Adam Gower, a trusted agent, who's worked with the Goodbarrels in the past. He will coordinate with Umli to have arrows and a shield made and teleported to you via Magical Courier. When they're ready, he'll also coordinate to hire a crew to begin breaking down the Flaming Tempest into useful timber, to sell the trade goods, to begin organizing people to hire to make plans, carpenters, architects, everybody who you'll need for the elaboration on Vindristjarna when you return.

before: DM: So I guess, having the Tollen background is, I didn't have time to make a lot of new backgrounds for this session, so we'll go with what I've got. Okay. So we begin tonight, the morning of January eighth as the sun shines on Vindristjarna, crossing high above the western hills of Cymea, approaching the presumed location of the cavern complex, known as the Edge of Echoes. Even with the mid-morning sun, the day is cold, at least this high up in the sky, with a light wind blowing from the western gulf.

DM: Faldrak has perched at the front of the ship, eagerly looking towards the horizon. He's wearing a thick silver gray woollen cloak over a battered, clearly ancient breastplate of sturdy, dwarven make, but clearly not worn or used in a while. He's leaning on his silver steel cane and on his shoulder the stone bird sits flapping, its wings uselessly, unable to fly. His long grey beard is braided with glittering beads that sparkle in the winter sun, and he seems quite thrilled to be on the move.

DM: So over the past few days—we'll come back to details as you all want to highlight them in your little stories—you've finished your business in Tollen, at least, for now. And said your goodbyes with hope to return soon.
after: DM: So in addition to this, this business, of course, you've all had your own goodbyes to say and things to do in these roughly 2 and a half days in Tollen. So anybody who has character moments they'd like to share? Now is the time. He's—
Unknown: Okay.
DM: Anybody?

Seeker: So I've I've just a handful of things. The interval of quiet and rest was an occasion for Seeker to ponder the nature of time and wonder about its relation to the planes, recalling the ancient lore known by all dwarven schoolchildren, of course, that time began at the moment of separation of the planes. And thinking about connections between the planes and those who would wish to cross boundaries between them. What might happen if the planes were brought back together again? Is that a way to stop time?

Seeker: At any rate, thinking about time, also got Seeker thinking about his family. And so he's written a letter updating his parents on his travels, occasionally amazed by his own densely packed adventures, and also asking for any—were there details that you recall about brother’s disappearance? We are hopefully doing investigation.

interactions.title: The Guild’s letter about Frankar
lines: DM: Flies up right next to Seeker, and it unrolls itself, unfolds itself into a piece of paper. Air mail. It is. It is a letter. It's the Philosophers’ Guild. And it says—there are words. It says, "Dear Seeker of Highkeep, brother to Frankar."

DM: Your gift, though generously given, is a common trinket device made in great numbers during the age of Drankor to facilitate logistical support for the armies of the Empire. The trick of their easy construction has been lost, but many 100 still survive. And there's little new to learn from this trinket.
DM: Nonetheless, your eagerness to understand the fate of your brother is noble, and some answers are not difficult to come by. So these now I share with you.

DM: Your brother, Frankar, was indeed seen alive on the elemental plane of fire some years ago, when exactly, I cannot say, but at least 5 years ago, by the standard reckoning of your people. It is said, a curious dwarf, bearing remarkable resemblance to your description of Frankar, was sighted within the illustrious city of Bronzehall, in the company of an efreet known as Zephyra. Whether he was willingly traveling with this creature or a captive was not clear, and the nature of their association—association is, and was, elusive.

DM: While the efreeti are often cruel, they do greatly value those who possess rare talent, so perhaps one can hope, he was travelling as a trusted advisor and not a slave. They were heading, according to those who saw them, towards the Cinder Wastes. Some claim they sought knowledge of the Oracle's Pyre, though what such a thing was or is, is not known to me beyond the obvious link from the name with both fire and divination magic.

DM: More than this I cannot say. Perhaps those who saw him in particular, the Azer may have more to report, should you wish to travel to the elemental plane of fire in the city of Bronzehall, and question them yourself. Signed, a Flame Warden, on behalf of the Ancient and Honorable Guild of Philosophers.

Seeker: What does that mean? Hmm. Must be one of the Philosophers’ Guild members that does something to do with flame. Intriguing. I think we will have to investigate this further at a future date. ((Other details))

And he clicks his heels together and does a little like twirl in the air as he continues to fly down the passageway.

I'm I'm not thinking of the words quite right, but like, you know, hunting hunting some animal in its lair, and but not in the like, hunting it down and killing it sort of way. And like—
DM: I get it. Yep, they. They also let you pass.

before: DM: An iron door with number of sort of pulsating runes. Some kind of magical protection, magical barriers, magical... They don't feel like traps to you. But what do you really know?
Seeker: Can we read the runes?
DM: Well, you're not there. Just Wellby is there.
Unknown: How far ahead?
DM: Like a hundred feet.
after: DM: And as as you pass by the winds, only Kenzo still having them trail slightly, but fading as you continue to walk, you see, ahead the the dancing mists and swirling fogs that Wellby described. And everybody make a charisma saving throw with advantage. Tell me if you roll less than a 13.
Kenzo: 17.
Seeker: I rolled less than 13 both times.
Delwath: 27.
DM: Okay, let me see what Faldrak rolled here.

interactions.title: The Drankorian woman’s greeting
lines: DM: And as you as you step into this this small antechamber—stepping through the wall is a woman, maybe 60 or so, elegantly dressed in silk robes, with graying hair cut short, green eyes, and a sharp and angular face marked by like an old burn running from her left eye to her jaw line.

DM: She bowed slightly and speaks before you can say anything. Kenzo, you recognize this as Drankorian. Translated: "Greetings, visitors. I hope your journey was not too difficult. I look forward to consulting with you on your needs, but sadly I am indisposed at the moment. Until I return, my servant Claudio will tend to your needs. Please be comfortable, and I will be with you shortly." And as she finishes speaking she gives a slight bow. And then.

before: Unknown: Obvious.
Kenzo: Can we open the door?
DM: It's not locked.
Kenzo: What's on the other side?

DM: So you push the door open and you step through, and you see a dusty, ancient chamber, lit by 4 large permanent magical lights. Rusting iron hooks on the wall perhaps once held tapestries or other wall hangings long since rotted away. There's 3 doors. There's a large bronze door straight ahead of you, through which a faint reddish glow can be seen, carved with these same kinds of warding runes of control, to keep elemental chaos at bay. To your right a reinforced wooden door, now dried and mostly rotted away, through which a small complex of living quarters and a storeroom can be seen. And to the left an intact stone door unlocked but closed.
after: DM: And we will stop here before you explore the forge.
Kenzo: That'd be cool if that was like Dimitaur's hologram AI assistant.
DM: Well, when you finally get to Drankor maybe Dimitaur will also have a Programmed Illusion for you.
Seeker: It's fun to have a classic dungeon crawl, cause we have done that a few times, but it's been a while so.
Kenzo: Hey, really quick! Before we sign off.
